method: Each record was written after reading the cited threads and documents in the snapshot cache. Quotes are verbatim substrings of their source (checked by commons:check-records). Everything outside a quote is an authored description, not the source's words. Aliases are search vocabulary added by the record writer and are marked as such in the interface.

problems.title: The eMMC never appears in U-Boot, so there is nothing to back up
symptoms: ums shows only the SD card
aliases: only the sd card shows up
problems.statusNote: Fixed on several units by two different changes, each of which failed on at least one other unit. #99 and #36 are still open.

evidence.quote: Here it never initialises, so there is nothing to read.
evidence.says: A January unit fails at `mmc dev 1` in both Route U and Route S, so the host is not the cause.

evidence.quote: The no-HS patch, as you suggested, fixed it here.
evidence.says: Another January larger-eMMC unit with the same symptom recovered with the no-HS patch.

evidence.quote: fixed by `docs/patches/pf1007l-v2025.10-no-mmc-hs.patch` (4-bit, 26 MHz, no HS) plus the START STOP correction.
evidence.says: A merged unit report documents the no-HS fix together with START STOP and the warm-up SPL.

evidence.quote: it rules high-speed timing out on your unit, which narrows it down.
evidence.says: On a May 20260519 unit the no-HS patch did not help; the maintainer points to the 12 MHz low-power build instead.

evidence.quote: Result: rooted on PF1007L 20260519 (larger eMMC).
evidence.says: The same unit later rooted with the 12 MHz build and a one-sector edit.

evidence.quote: Rebuilt with start-stop + linux-12mhz patches (4-bit, 12 MHz, NO_PMIC, 408 MHz): UMS appeared read-only.
evidence.says: A second May unit exposed the eMMC with the 12 MHz build.

evidence.quote: Still unsolved, so leaving this open.
evidence.says: The original report remains open; neither fix has been tried there.

evidence.quote: U-Boot never initialises the eMMC
evidence.says: The maintainer's symptom table lists this row as Unsolved on #99 and names both fixes with their reports.

approaches.label: No-HS patch: legacy eMMC timing, 4-bit at 26 MHz
12 MHz low-power build (SUNXI_NO_PMIC, CPU 408 MHz)
approaches.scope: May 20260519 units where no-HS did not help

openQuestions: Why does no-HS fix some larger-eMMC units and not others with the same symptom?
Does #99's unit respond to either change? It has not tried them.

related.note: #99 names #16, #17 and #18 and calls its own failure different.
Both stop before any eMMC data reaches the host; the cause may or may not be shared.

decisions: Split from ums-drops-during-backup because the reporter of #99 explicitly distinguishes 'never initialises' from 'reads drop'.
Status is partly-solved, not solved: a fix that worked elsewhere is not a fix for #99.
uncertainty: Which hardware variable separates the two fixes is not established in any source.

problems.title: The backup disk appears, then drops or errors partway through reading
problems.statusNote: Several fixes are documented with reports; which one a unit needs is found by trying them in order.

evidence.quote: the drops traced to an eMMC read error inside U-Boot, with no USB traffic involved.
evidence.says: The drops were eMMC read errors in U-Boot, not a USB problem; 25 MHz read cleanly.

evidence.quote: Route U worked on macOS after two changes to the U-Boot build and moving the frame off a bus-powered hub.
evidence.says: Low-power build plus a direct port fixed drops on one unit.

evidence.quote: reads succeeded in **all** speed modes: legacy, HS, and HS52 capped at 12 MHz.
evidence.says: At 26 MHz every read failed; capping the eMMC at 12 MHz fixed all reads on a January unit.

evidence.quote: because the default build cannot read this eMMC.
evidence.says: A May 20260529 unit on Linux also needed the 12 MHz low-power build.

evidence.quote: Read errors, `ums` drops, slow or failing backup
evidence.says: The maintainer's table row lists 4-bit 26 MHz or 8-bit 25 MHz with its reports.

evidence.quote: Bulk eMMC reads fail even at 4-bit 26 MHz
evidence.says: When 26 MHz is not enough, the table points to the 12 MHz cap with the low-power build.

evidence.quote: Drops through a bus-powered hub
evidence.says: Power is a separate cause: direct port or powered hub.

approaches.label: Lower the eMMC to 4-bit 26 MHz (or 8-bit 25 MHz)
Cap the eMMC at 12 MHz with the low-power build
Direct port or powered hub; low-power build
approaches.scope: drops that follow a bus-powered hub

openQuestions: Is the larger eMMC itself, or its board wiring, the reason full speed fails?

related.note: The maintainer's table lists START STOP and clock changes as separate rows with overlapping reports.
Same symptom with a host-side cause, listed in the same table.

decisions: One record for the read-failure family; the maintainer's table splits it into several rows by which fix applied.
uncertainty: Reports differ in host, cable and firmware at once, so no single variable is isolated.

problems.title: The disk vanishes about 45 seconds after U-Boot starts, or when the computer ejects it
symptoms: frame resets to FEL ~45-50 s after Starting U-Boot
problems.statusNote: The reporter confirmed the START STOP patch fixed it; the maintainer moved the fix into the table.

evidence.quote: the frame resets
evidence.says: Both disks enumerate, then the frame drops back to FEL 45 to 50 seconds later, every time.

evidence.quote: Confirmed fix: the START STOP patch from #28 solved the 45–50 s reset on my unit.
evidence.says: The reporter confirms the fix and a full verified backup.

evidence.quote: look like a different problem and are listed separately there.
evidence.says: Resets without ums, on April and May units, are kept apart as a different problem.

evidence.quote: The disk disappears when the computer sends "eject" or "stop"
evidence.says: The table's fix: ignore START STOP UNIT unless it is a real unload.

approaches.label: START STOP patch: ignore eject and stop unless it is a real unload
approaches.scope: Route U ums on any host that ejects

related.note: The maintainer separates resets with and without ums.

decisions: Merged 'resets at 45 s' and 'eject' into one record because one patch fixed both.
uncertainty: Why a stop command makes the frame reset, rather than only unmount, is not explained in the sources.

evidence.quote: Route S refuses it by design.
evidence.says: The hash is a known 20260416 image, not new firmware; try the gentler routes first.

evidence.quote: I finally succeeded by creating a USB drive and booting my PC via Linux to set up a Wi-Fi hotspot, etc.
evidence.says: The reporter succeeded another way; the thread does not say which route, and the issue stays open.

problems.title: The frame shows no USB data, or no power, on the computer
symptoms: frame does not power on from a USB-C hub
problems.statusNote: Documented as a rule, with a qualification the maintainer added: the rule is a reliable start, not proof.

evidence.quote: A USB-C to USB-C cable gave unit C **no power and no data**.
evidence.says: The frame appears to lack the USB-C CC pull-downs, so use a USB-A to USB-C data cable.

evidence.quote: Treat the cable recommendation as a reliable starting point, rather than proof
evidence.says: A May Mac report saw intermittent C-to-C data through a hub; CC wiring was not measured.

evidence.quote: Update: it was the cable.
evidence.says: A 'no USB data' report turned out to be a C-to-C cable; with another cable the frame enumerated.

evidence.quote: The cable bundled with the frame carried no data
evidence.says: The cable in the box was charge-only.

evidence.quote: a USB-C to USB-C cable direct to the Mac gave **no power and no USB data at all**
evidence.says: A Frameo ZC002, a different brand, behaved the same way.

approaches.label: USB-A to USB-C cable known to carry data, into a USB-A port

openQuestions: Do these boards really lack CC pull-down resistors? Nobody has measured it.

decisions: Cross-device: the same symptom was reported on a Frameo board.
uncertainty: The CC explanation is the maintainer's inference, stated as 'appears to'.

evidence.quote: one persisted property made root ADB over USB survive reboots, with no boot partition write
